 Public urged to exercise caution near rivers, waterfalls during monsoon
 By FARIK ZOLKEPLI 
 Wednesday, 11 Nov 2026
 | 9:35 AM MYT

 KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians have been urged to exercise extreme caution when engaging in recreational activities near rivers and waterfalls during the Northeast Monsoon following a tragedy in Kuala Kubu Baru.
 Alliance for a Safe Community chairman Tan Sri Lee Lam Thye said the incident, in which several people were reportedly swept away by strong currents, with search-and-rescue operations continuing for the missing, was a stark reminder of the dangers posed by sudden water surges, commonly known as kepala air.
 He said such incidents could occur when heavy rainfall upstream caused river levels to rise rapidly, even when weather conditions at the recreational site appeared fine.
 "My heartfelt condolences go to the families of the victims. I also commend the Fire and Rescue Department and all emergency personnel involved in the search-and-rescue operation," he said in a statement on Wednesday (Nov 11).
 Lee advised the public to avoid swimming, bathing, picnicking and camping near rivers, waterfalls and rapids during periods of heavy rainfall.
 He also urged hikers and campers to check weather forecasts before embarking on outdoor activities, stay away from riverbanks and move immediately to higher ground when conditions became unsafe.
 The public should also be alert to warning signs such as sudden changes in water levels, muddy water, stronger currents and floating debris.
 However, Lee cautioned that people should not wait for these signs before taking precautionary action, as sudden water surges could occur very quickly.
 "Authorities should strengthen preventive measures by temporarily closing high-risk recreational sites during adverse weather conditions.
 "Other measures should include installing early warning systems, such as water-level monitoring equipment and warning sirens, as well as ensuring campsite and recreational operators had proper emergency evacuation plans," he added.
 Lee also called for better coordination among the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), Fire and Rescue Department, local authorities, Forestry Department and recreational-site operators to ensure timely warnings and effective enforcement of safety measures.
 He proposed that Malaysia work towards achieving a national "Zero Drowning and Zero Preventable Deaths" objective during the monsoon season, stressing that this would require a collective commitment from the authorities, recreational operators and the public.
 "No recreational activity is worth risking human lives. Public safety must always take precedence over enjoyment and convenience.
 "Do not wait until the water rises before deciding to leave. By then, it may already be too late. Prevention, preparedness and responsible behaviour can save lives," he said.
